ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A sofa with a mass of $m=30\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on a horizontal ground. Xiao Hong pushes the sofa with a horizontal force parallel to the ground. When the pushing force is $F_1=80\mathrm{N}$, the sofa remains stationary. When the pushing force is $F_2=120\mathrm{N}$, the sofa moves at a constant velocity. The gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^2$.

1. The sofa is subjected to a frictional force of magnitude $f_1$ under the action of an 80N pushing force.
2. The coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu$ between the sofa and the ground.
3. The sofa, under a thrust of 140N, experiences a frictional force of magnitude $f_2$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Text-only problem; no image evidence is needed. Apply separate force-balance conditions for each stated motion state. 1. For the 80 N push, the sofa remains stationary, so the horizontal resultant force is zero. Static friction adjusts to balance the applied push. Therefore f1 = 80 N. 2. For the 120 N push, the sofa moves at constant velocity, so the horizontal resultant force is also zero. Thus the kinetic friction force equals 120 N. On horizontal ground with only vertical forces weight and normal force, N = mg = 30 × 10 = 300 N. The kinetic friction coefficient is μ = fk / N = 120 / 300 = 0.4. 3. For a 140 N push while the sofa is sliding, the kinetic friction is determined by μN, not by the applied force. Hence f2 = μN = 0.4 × 300 = 120 N.
